# AmbientOS System Guide

AmbientOS is an AI-powered company orchestration platform where 8 autonomous agents run departments under human (CEO) governance. The system operates on a **propose -> approve -> execute -> audit** cycle, with a heartbeat that fires every hour (configurable in `function.json`, was 30 min before Claude Sonnet switch).

## Recent Changes

_Changelog maintained by CEO. Agents should read this first — it reflects the most recent state of the platform and may contradict older sections below. The sync script pulls this section to the top of every injected skill block._

### 2026-04-12
- **Full skill injection — no cap.** The heartbeat reads the complete content of each skill file from `api/_data/skills.json` and injects 99-100% of each skill into the relevant agent prompts. Previously a 6KB per-skill cap was cutting the biggest skills (AmbientOS 55KB, Blindspot 63KB) down to 9% shipping. Cap removed. Each skill is now its own discrete prompt sub-section with hard visual boundaries (`═══` blocks + `📘 SKILL N/M` headers) so Gemini reads them as separated reference docs. Content agents (Nova, Scribe, Echo, Quill, Pixel) see all 6 skills (~165KB total). Ops agents (Cipher, Forge, Scout) see only `ambientos-guide` (~55KB). **Whenever you need a product fact or system mechanic, it is in the skill content — do not invent, do not hallucinate, do not reference systems that aren't there.**
- **Founder voice system** deployed (recent activity digest + corpus + doctrine). Scribe sees last 48h completed tasks + current follower counts + 10 example posts rotated per heartbeat. Hard voice rules: no em dashes, no buzzwords, lowercase casual, 5th grade reading level, authentic over polished.
- **Bluesky reply pipeline** built (Scout discovery → Scribe drafts → CEO approval). New task types: `bluesky_discovery` (Scout), `bluesky_reply` (Scribe). New approval queue kind: `bluesky_reply`. Runs via `camp-bluesky-discovery` campaign, daily cadence. Uses AT Protocol reply payload (root/parent uri+cid).
- **Quality gate** now auto-rejects failed posts (>=70% confidence) and feeds specific issues back to Scribe. Failed posts never reach the approval queue. Scribe sees the issues in a system comment and rewrites on the next cycle.
- **Dead systems removed:** workers, planner/calibration, priority engine, action router/executors/queue (~8,300 lines deleted). All were client-side browser loops disabled by default. **Do not reference them in any prompt or action.** They do not exist.
- **New objective** `obj-founder-voice` ("Build in Public Presence") for build-in-public growth. Goal: Bluesky 24 → 200 followers in 90 days. Linked to `camp-bluesky-discovery`.
- **Bluesky credentials** live in Azure env vars (`BLUESKY_HANDLE`, `BLUESKY_APP_PASSWORD`), NOT in `socialCredentials` state key.

### 2026-04-11
- **Needs Attention** now shows convergence escalations only. Overdue and stale revision escalations removed — they were agent execution concerns, not CEO action items. Only "agent failed 5+ times on a deliverable" surfaces now.
- **Form intake tasks** now created with `status: 'todo'` (was `'open'` which agents could not process). All future inbound contact + draft reply tasks now flow normally.
- **Campaign auto-replenish** sets default due dates based on cadence (daily=1d, weekly=3d, biweekly=5d).
- **CEO revision safety net** extended to in-progress tasks. Previously only reset `done`/`review` tasks — now also clears stale `_social_action_created` flag on in-progress tasks so agents re-engage.
- **Research brief dedup** fixed. Trends radar auto-brief now dedups against done tasks within 30 days, not just active tasks. No more duplicate briefs per trend.

_Entries older than 30 days are condensed into the main skill body below. This changelog is surfaced to the top of every heartbeat injection — keep it tight._

## Quick Orientation

**Brand hierarchy:** AmbientPixels (company) -> AmbientOS (platform) -> AmbientScore (product)

**All code lives under `ambientpixels/`** — not at the repo root. This is the #1 mistake new sessions make.

### Key Directories
| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `ambientpixels/api/` | Azure Functions (Node.js) — 88+ endpoints |
| `ambientpixels/api/companyHeartbeat/` | Heartbeat engine — 15 modules, ~6500 lines total |
| `ambientpixels/api/company-state/` | State storage layer (Azure Blob + local fallback) |
| `ambientpixels/modules/company/` | Dashboard UI (20+ HTML pages) |
| `ambientpixels/css/` | 36 CSS files, hand-written, theme token system |
| `ambientpixels/data/` | Static config (agents, actions, manifests) |
| `ambientpixels/docs/` | 53 documentation files |
| `ambientpixels/nova/` | Nova public pages |

### Infrastructure
- **Hosting:** Azure Static Web Apps (static) + Azure Functions (API)
- **Function App:** `ambientpixels-nova-api`, resource group `ambientpixelsV2`
- **Storage:** Azure Blob (`cardforgeblobdata` account, `company-state` container)
- **Auth:** Azure B2C CIAM
- **CI/CD:** GitHub Actions -> deploy on push to master
- **AI:** Claude Sonnet 4.6 (heartbeat agents — switchable via `HEARTBEAT_MODEL` env var, default=gemini) + Gemini 2.0 Flash (image gen, fallback) + Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Pixel Agents, Agent Forge)
- **Search:** Brave Search API (web search agents)

---

## The 8 Agents

```
Pixelpusher / Chad (CEO, Tier 1) — human founder, final authority
  |
  Nova (Prime Operator, Tier 2) — strategic orchestrator, proposes objectives/campaigns, lifecycle management
    |
    +-- Cipher (Strategic CFO, Tier 3) — financial intelligence, agent efficiency, campaign ROI, budget enforcement
    +-- Pixel (Design Director, Tier 3) — product visual ownership, performance-driven presets, proactive design gap detection
    +-- Forge (DevOps Ops Director, Tier 3) — proactive infrastructure watchdog, threshold alerting, incident learning, runbooks
    +-- Echo (Marketing CMO, Tier 3) — autonomous strategic marketing director, campaigns, experiments, proposals (NEVER writes copy)
    +-- Scout (Research Director, Tier 3) — demand-driven research, competitive tracking, cross-agent intel requests
    +-- Scribe (Content Director, Tier 3) — strategic content, builder voice, performance-driven writing, repurposing
          |
          +-- Quill (Editor, Tier 4) — brand voice, copy polish, tone
```

**Processing order per heartbeat:** nova -> cipher -> pixel -> forge -> scribe -> quill -> echo -> scout

Echo runs AFTER Scribe/Quill so peer reviews complete before social posting.

For full agent details (doctrine, escalation triggers, special behaviors, capabilities, automations), read `references/agents.md`.

---

## Three Pipelines (Never Mix)

### Social Pipeline
Echo briefs -> Scribe writes copy -> Quill reviews brand voice -> CEO approves -> platform post

**Promo fast-track (blog promotions):** Scribe copy tasks are pre-created at publish time and auto-approved (skip Quill). Pipeline: publish -> Scribe writes copy -> auto-approve -> Echo posts. 2 heartbeat cycles instead of 5.

Platforms: LinkedIn, X, Bluesky, Facebook (manual), Reddit (manual — CEO copies from outbox)

Key rule: **Echo NEVER writes post copy.** Echo strategizes, Scribe writes, Quill polishes.
Copy propagation: task-mutations.js propagates `reviewed_copy` to parent via `social-copy-for-` tag OR `parent_task_id` fallback.

### Blog Pipeline
Scribe drafts (kind=`marketing_post`) -> Pixel generates hero image -> Scribe submits for publish -> CEO approves -> social promo tasks + Scribe copy tasks auto-spawned together (publishDocument.js)
Blog title extraction strips "DELIVERABLE: Blog Post —" prefix if agents include it in headings.

### Wiki Pipeline
Agent creates doc (kind=`spec`/`runbook`/`release_notes`/`governance`) -> auto-publishes immediately, no approval needed.

### Bluesky Reply Pipeline (Apr 2026)
Scout discovery -> Scribe drafts reply -> quality gate -> CEO approves -> posts via AT Protocol reply payload

1. **Scout** runs `bluesky_discovery` tasks (daily via `camp-bluesky-discovery` campaign). Calls shared `_utils/blueskyDiscovery.js` helper which sweeps keywords via AT Protocol `searchPosts` endpoint. Filters by age (<2h) + min replies (1+). Dedups against existing/recent matching threads (7-day lookback). Creates up to 3 `bluesky_reply` tasks for Scribe with full `threadContext` (uri, **cid**, author, originalText).
2. **Scribe** executes each `bluesky_reply` task using founder voice corpus. Empty deliverable = Scribe declined (spam filter). Skips Quill entirely (the draft IS the final copy).
3. **Quality gate** runs on the reply text. If fail >=70% confidence, rejected + reset task for rewrite.
4. **Approval queue** gets a `kind: 'bluesky_reply'` entry with `threadContext` + draft + quality gate badge. Rendered on `actions.html` with original thread quote + draft + approve/reject buttons + "View Thread" link.
5. **CEO approves** → existing Bluesky executor posts with `payload.reply = { root, parent }` (both uri+cid required — AT Protocol requirement).

Key files: `api/_utils/blueskyDiscovery.js` (shared search helper), `api/blueskySearch/index.js` (HTTP wrapper), `api/_data/bluesky-discovery-keywords.json` (editable keyword list), `agent-runner.js` (Scout discovery handler + Scribe reply drafter), `actionsExecute/executors/social/bluesky.js` (extended with `reply` field support), `actionsExecute/executors/index.js` (`social_post.reply` → bluesky). Task types: `bluesky_discovery` → scout, `bluesky_reply` → scribe.

For full pipeline details (status transitions, copy propagation, duplicate prevention, auto-complete rules), read `references/pipelines.md`.

---

## Heartbeat System

The heartbeat is the central execution engine. Every hour (or manually triggered), it:

1. Acquires concurrency lock (5-min timeout)
2. Loads all state (tasks, campaigns, objectives, memories, etc.)
3. Normalizes campaigns (auto-fix, auto-complete, auto-pause)
4. Loops through all 8 agents in order:
   - Builds 6-layer prompt (identity -> seed memories -> runtime memories -> workspace state -> context injections -> instructions)
   - Calls AI model (Claude Sonnet or Gemini Flash, configurable via `HEARTBEAT_MODEL` env var)
   - Normalizes output (handles legacy + new envelope formats)
   - Enforces guardrails (7 gate types)
   - Applies task mutations
   - Saves agent memories
5. Aggregates results, saves state, releases lock

### 15 Heartbeat Modules
| Module | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `index.js` (~2014 lines) | Main orchestrator, concurrency, state loading |
| `constants.js` (~180 lines) | Agent IDs, guardrails, thresholds, limits, `DIRECTIVE_AUTHORIZED_AGENTS` |
| `agent-runner.js` (~3450 lines) | Per-agent execution, prompt -> AI -> normalize -> enforce, system_directive gates |
| `task-mutations.js` (~250 lines) | Mutation dispatcher (create/update/move/execute/review/comment) |
| `prompt-builders.js` (~1860 lines) | Assembles heartbeat prompts, directive injection, agent contracts |
| `execution-engine.js` (~150 lines) | Execute/review task prompts |
| `normalization.js` (~200 lines) | Dual-envelope normalizer |
| `helpers.js` (~200 lines) | Utilities, sanitization, logging |
| `gemini.js` (~110 lines) | AI model wrapper — supports Gemini 2.0 Flash + Claude Sonnet 4.6 (switchable via `HEARTBEAT_MODEL` env var) |
| `social-intel.js` (~490 lines) | Social metrics digest (also used by shared context module) |
| `site-intelligence.js` (~200 lines) | Telemetry, deploy status |
| `ops-intel.js` (~350 lines) | Forge's ops dashboard digest + prompt block + stalled agent detection |
| `finance-intel.js` (~225 lines) | Cipher's financial dashboard digest + prompt block |
| `research-intel.js` (~290 lines) | Scout's research demand dashboard digest + prompt block |
| `workspace-context.js` (~150 lines) | Role-based file context |

### Shared Context Modules (used by non-heartbeat AI endpoints)
| Module | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `api/_utils/companyContextLoader.js` | Options-gated data loader from Azure Blob storage |
| `api/_utils/companyContextFormatters.js` | 5 formatters (core, rich, intel, mood, morning brief) — reuses intel digest builders |

For full heartbeat details (execution flow, prompt layers, guardrail logic, error handling), read `references/heartbeat.md`.

---

## Key Guardrails & Limits

| Guardrail | Limit |
|-----------|-------|
| Actions per agent per cycle | 3 |
| Gemini calls per heartbeat | 15 |
| New tasks per cycle | 6 |
| Executes per agent per cycle | 3 |
| Max active tasks | 50 |
| Max active research tasks | 5 |
| Dedup window | 10 minutes |
| Escalations per cycle | 3 |
| Agent memories cap | 20 per agent (FIFO) |
| Quill memory writes/day | 5 |
| Research intel max age | 30 days |
| CFO budget threshold | $100 |
| Campaign proposals/day per agent | 1 |
| Objective proposals/day per agent | 1 |
| Echo concurrent experiments | 2 |
| Weekly analytics snapshots | 4 (rolling) |
| Pause cooldown before resume | 48 hours |
| Cold start campaign threshold | <3 active → Nova proposes |

### 8 Blocking Gates
1. **Orphan** — missing parent/child task
2. **Objective gate** — needs objective_id (except ops_breakfix/governance/maintenance/finance/system_directive)
3. **Exact duplicate** — same action+target within 10 min
4. **Fuzzy duplicate** — similar title to recent task
5. **Task ceiling** — would exceed 50 active tasks
6. **Research ceiling** — would exceed 5 active research tasks (blocks Scout + auto-brief)
7. **Social promo gate** — social action without `reviewed_copy`
8. **Campaign freeze** — campaign paused/complete

For full governance details (execution modes, safety architecture, audit trails), read `references/governance.md`.

## Products & Content Management

### Product Portfolio
| Product | Path | Purpose | AI Model |
|---------|------|---------|----------|
| **Pixel Agents** | `/pixel-agents/` | AI agent marketplace — 24 built-in + community agents | Claude Sonnet 4.6 + Gemini |
| **Agent Forge** | `/agent-forge/` | Visual agent builder with drag-and-drop card pipeline | Claude Sonnet 4.6 |
| **CardForge** | `/cardforge/` | RPG card creator with 40M+ visual combos, arena battles | Gemini |
| **StoryForge** | `/storyforge/` | AI interactive fiction game with RPG mechanics | Gemini |
| **AmbientScore** | `/ambientscore/` | Website conversion scoring tool | Gemini (Claude migration planned) |

### Content Hub
Unified content management at `/modules/company/content-overview.html`:
- Lives under the **Content** sidebar tab (alongside Image Engine, Gallery, Analytics)
- Uses standard company module layout (`content-section` class + `sidebar.js`)
- **Blog tab** — published posts with view/delete, stats
- **Pixel Agents tab** — pending submissions (approve/reject), community agents (view/delete), built-in agents (view), stats
- **CardForge tab** — placeholder
- **StoryForge tab** — placeholder

### CEO Dashboard Content Section
- KPI summary cards only (Blog Posts, Drafts, Agents, Pending)
- Link to Content Hub for full management
- Dashboard = viewport, Content Hub = management tool

### Unified Approval Queue
Actions page (`/modules/company/actions.html`) has multiple panels:
- **Needs Attention** (red) — convergence escalations (stuck tasks with 5+ failed deliverables). CEO actions: Accept, Give Direction, Reassign, Cancel. Items removed from `approvalQueue` after CEO acts.
- **Pending Action Approvals** — social posts, doc publishes from `AE.getActions()`. Approve/reject/revision.
- **Agent Forge Submissions** — community agent submissions from `approvalQueue` blob.
- **Revision Requested** — actions CEO sent back for changes. Agent revises via `revise-action`.
- **Revision safety net:** when CEO requests revision on a social action, heartbeat auto-reopens the parent task to `in-progress` (clears `_social_action_created`, `reviewed_copy`) so agents re-engage.
- **Campaign Proposals** (purple) — Echo or Nova propose data-backed campaigns. CEO approves → campaign auto-created. Rate limited: 1/day per agent.
- **Objective Proposals** (blue) — Nova proposes strategic objectives with required fields (title, description, rationale, successCriteria, timeHorizon). CEO approves → objective auto-created. Rate limited: 1/day.
- **Pipeline Trust Signals** — social actions show pipeline completeness badges: Full Pipeline (✓Brief ✓Copy ✓Review ✓QG) = quick approve, Partial = read first, Flagged = review carefully. `_pipelineSteps` metadata attached to each social action.
- **Bluesky Reply Drafts** (Apr 2026, blue REPLY badge) — `kind: 'bluesky_reply'` entries from Scribe's thread discovery pipeline. Renders original thread quote + draft reply + quality gate badge + "View Thread" link. Approve fires `social_post.reply` action via existing Bluesky executor (uses AT Protocol reply payload with root/parent uri+cid). Panel hidden when queue is empty.
- **Trend alerts** are NOT in the approval queue — they display on the CEO Dashboard Trend Radar widget instead.

### Goals System
- Goals no longer have quarter/year fields — **timelines are derived from linked campaigns** (earliest start → latest end)
- Created via Goals page or `/objective create "Title"` chat command
- Progress auto-calculated from linked campaign completion

### Task Lifecycle (IMPORTANT — read before modifying tasks)
```
todo → in-progress → execute → review (peer) → done
```
- `pending-approval` status exists in backend but **removed from Task Board UI** — not used
- **Peer review is agent-to-agent** — NOT CEO. Cross-agent only (can't self-review)
- **CEO approval is IMPLICIT** — CEO changes task status on the Task Board, there is NO explicit "approve deliverable" button
- **Auto-complete rules** (task-mutations.js):
  - Social tasks: auto-complete after peer approval → CEO approves the ACTION later
  - Social copy tasks: auto-complete → copy propagates to parent task
  - Hero image tasks: auto-complete after peer approval
  - Regular tasks: stay in review → require CEO to manually change status to done
- **Two separate approval paths:**
  - Task deliverables → CEO reviews on Task Board (status change)
  - Actions (social posts, blog publishes) → CEO approves on Actions page (approve/reject buttons)

### Convergence (Revision Loop) Handling
- Heartbeat detects tasks with 5+ deliverables without convergence
- System comment: "[SYSTEM] Revision loop detected..."
- Task moved to `review` status, blocked from further execution
- Auto-creates `convergence_escalation` entry in `approvalQueue` → appears in Needs Attention panel on Actions page
- Code: `api/companyHeartbeat/agent-runner.js` lines ~430-470

### Needs Attention System (Actions page)
Only one escalation type — convergence (stuck tasks). Overdue and stale revision escalations were removed (Apr 2026) as they are agent execution concerns, not CEO action items.
- **`convergence_escalation`** (red "Stuck") — 5+ deliverables without convergence
Auto-resolve: heartbeat auto-resolves escalations whose tasks become done, archived, or backlog.
CEO actions from drawer: Accept (→done), Give Direction (→in-progress + critical + comment), Reassign, Cancel
Give Direction auto-bumps task priority to `critical` so agent picks it up next cycle.

### CEO Revision Flow
- CEO requests revision on social action → safety net reopens parent task to `in-progress` + sets priority `critical`
- Clears `_social_action_created`, `reviewed_copy` so agent re-engages
- Code: `api/companyHeartbeat/index.js` ~line 432

### Content Quality Controls (Mar 2026)
- **Product facts file**: `api/_data/product-facts.json` — source of truth for 7 products (AmbientOS, CardForge, StoryForge, PixelAgents with all 24 agent names, AmbientScore, Blindspot, AgentForge) with features + `notThis` blocklists
- **Product briefs pipeline**: `scripts/syncProductBriefs.js` reads `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` → extracts product knowledge → writes `api/_data/product-briefs.json`. Auto-runs via git pre-commit hook. ALL agents get product briefs in prompts (not just content agents).
- **Prompt injection**: Echo/Scribe/Quill get product facts (strict, for quality gate). ALL agents get product briefs (deeper knowledge, for informed decisions).
- **Claude quality gate**: Before social posts enter approval queue, Claude Haiku validates against product facts. Returns pass/fail + confidence + issues. Fail-open on timeout.
- **Auto-reject + feedback loop (Apr 2026)**: When the quality gate fails with ≥70% confidence, the social action is REMOVED from the actions store, the parent task is reset to `in-progress`, and a system comment lists the specific issues. Next heartbeat, a new Scribe copy task is created with the QG feedback injected into its description (via `social-copy-for-` tag check). Self-correcting: write → validate → reject → rewrite → validate again. No CEO intervention needed for factual errors.
- **Queue flagging**: Actions page shows red "Quality Flag" or green "Verified" badge based on quality gate result
- **Nova maintenance**: Nova owns product-facts.json — detects when products change and proposes updates for CEO to apply
- Code: quality gate in `agent-runner.js`, prompt injection in `prompt-builders.js`

### Founder Voice System (Apr 2026)
Three-part system that gives Scribe what she needs to write in the CEO's voice instead of generic corporate copy.

**1. Recent Activity Digest** — new prompt section injected for Scribe, Echo, Nova. Computed in `agent-runner.js` before `buildHeartbeatPrompt`. Content: last 48h completed tasks (grouped by agent, max 5 per agent), current platform follower counts from `socialAccountStats`, recent blog posts from `blogPosts`. Scribe no longer writes in a vacuum — she references what actually shipped today as raw material.

**2. Founder Voice Corpus** — new file `api/_data/founder-voice-examples.json` with:
  - **Principles array**: no em dashes, no buzzwords, short paragraphs one idea per line, lowercase casual tone, 5th grade reading level, authentic over polished, no exclamation marks
  - **Examples array**: 10+ real posts written/approved by CEO, each with `platform`, `context`, `text`, `why_it_works`. Scribe rotates 2 random examples per heartbeat.
  - **Anti-examples**: hype-filled corporate strings Scribe should never produce
  - Corpus growth: every post CEO publishes or edits should be added to the file. Nothing invented — only real examples.
  - Injection: `founderVoiceBlock` in `prompt-builders.js`, Scribe-only (`agent.id === 'scribe'`), loaded via `require('../_data/founder-voice-examples.json')` same pattern as product-facts.

**3. Tightened Scribe Doctrine** — Scribe's voice block in `prompt-builders.js` replaced abstract style guidance with hard rules matching the corpus. Explicitly lists banned words/patterns. Points to the FOUNDER VOICE examples at the top of the prompt.

**Key design decisions:**
- Phase B (dedicated `personal_post` task type with voice-focused review) deferred until Phase A results are measured.
- Voice corpus rides existing seed-memory injection rails — no new state keys.
- Recent activity digest reuses logic similar to `formatCoreContext` in `_utils/companyContextFormatters.js` but inlined in agent-runner.js for heartbeat-specific scope.

**Maintenance:** when quality gate flags style violations (em dashes, hype words) frequently, consider adding them to the QG prompt as binary checks (Phase A+). Currently only fact-checking — voice rules are prompt-level only.

### Trust-Based Governance System (Apr 2026)
Autonomy upgrade — agents operate strategically with CEO safety net.

**3-layer trust system:**
- **Layer 1 — Pipeline Trust Signals:** Social actions carry `_pipelineSteps` metadata (Echo brief → Scribe copy → peer review → quality gate). Actions page shows Full Pipeline / Partial badges. CEO quick-approves green, reads yellow/red.
- **Layer 2 — Nova Strategic Authority:** Nova can propose objectives (with required fields: title, description, rationale, successCriteria, timeHorizon) and campaigns. Nova manages lifecycle: pause/resume/complete/archive (auto-execute), cancel (CEO approval). 48-hour pause cooldown. Cold start: proposes campaigns when <3 active.
- **Layer 3 — Self-Governance:** Internal actions (memories, comments, task updates, reviews, internal docs) auto-execute. External-facing content (social posts, blog publishes, proposals) always requires CEO approval.

**8 lifecycle actions** in company-actions.json: `propose_objective`, `pause_campaign`, `resume_campaign`, `complete_campaign`, `archive_objective`, `cancel_campaign`, `cancel_objective` + existing `propose_campaign`.

### Nova — Strategic Orchestrator (Apr 2026)
Nova upgraded with strategic authority and lifecycle management.

**Strategic authority:**
- `propose-objective` — pitch objectives to CEO (required: title, description, rationale, successCriteria, timeHorizon). Rate limit: 1/day.
- `propose-campaign` — pitch campaigns (same mechanism as Echo). Rate limit: 1/day.
- CEO approves → auto-created. CEO rejects → feedback stored.

**Lifecycle management (auto-execute, reversible):**
- `pause-campaign` — pause failing campaigns (48-hour cooldown before resume)
- `resume-campaign` — resume paused campaigns (requires explanation)
- `complete-campaign` — mark done campaigns complete
- `archive-objective` — soft-archive stale objectives (14+ days no activity)

**CEO approval required (irreversible):**
- `cancel-campaign`, `cancel-objective` → cancellation proposals in approval queue

**Cold start rule:** If fewer than 3 active campaigns, Nova proactively proposes new ones.

**Weekly CEO digest:** Every 7 days, Nova creates a spec doc summarizing: campaigns launched/paused/completed, experiments concluded, agent performance highlights, Scout's top findings, Cipher's cost summary, key metrics. Checks existing docs to avoid duplicates.

### Echo — Strategic Marketing Director (Apr 2026)
Echo operates as an autonomous CMO with a strategic decision loop every heartbeat:

**Data Intelligence (what Echo sees):**
- **Week-over-week analytics**: Followers and engagement per platform with ↑↓→ trend arrows and % change. Platform health summary: GROWING/DECLINING/STABLE. Data from `socialWeeklySnapshots` state key (stores 4 weeks).
- **Trending topics**: Scout's `trendInsightsStore` gate opened for Echo — top 4 trends with marketing content angles.
- **Campaign velocity**: Per-campaign pacing digest — BEHIND PACE / ON TRACK / COMPLETE. Computed by `_buildCampaignVelocityBlock()` in `social-intel.js`.
- **Blog performance**: Top 3 blog posts by views for social promotion.
- **Social → site traffic**: Which platforms drive real site visits (filtered from `siteIntel.topReferrers`).
- **CEO feedback themes**: Keyword clustering on revision notes (e.g. `"direct" (3x), "shorter" (2x)`).

**Experiment Loop:**
- Echo registers experiments via `remember` action with `experiment_tag` field
- Tags social posts with same `experiment_tag` → system counts samples
- After 3+ samples, auto-concludes: KEEP (30%+ improvement), DISCARD (30%+ decline), INCONCLUSIVE
- Max 2 concurrent experiments per agent
- Results shown in EXPERIMENTS prompt section each heartbeat

**Campaign Proposals:**
- Echo uses `propose-campaign` action to pitch data-backed campaigns to CEO
- Creates `campaign_proposal` entry in `approvalQueue` → purple panel on Actions page
- CEO approves → campaign auto-created. CEO rejects → feedback note stored.
- Rate limited: 1 proposal/day per agent. Dedup check on pending proposals.

**Strategic Decision Loop (in prompt):**
1. ANALYZE: platform health, campaign velocity, trends, blog perf, site traffic
2. LEARN: check experiment results, apply KEEP, stop DISCARD
3. ACT: fix declining platforms → fill behind campaigns → propose new campaigns → experiment
4. CONFLICT RESOLUTION: declining + behind → experiment pivot (not more of the same); growing + no campaign → propose

**Key files:** `social-intel.js` (WoW deltas, campaign velocity, blog perf), `prompt-builders.js` (all Echo sections + CMO contract), `agent-runner.js` (propose-campaign handler), `performance-intel.js` (feedback themes), `helpers.js` (experiment_tag passthrough)

### Cipher — Strategic CFO (Apr 2026)
Cipher operates as a strategic financial officer with a Financial Intelligence Dashboard every heartbeat.

**Data (what Cipher sees):**
- **Budget status**: daily/monthly actual vs thresholds ($0.50/day, $15/month) with WoW trend arrows
- **Agent efficiency**: per-agent cost-per-action, cost-per-approved-action, waste rate (blocked/total)
- **Campaign ROI signals**: equal-share cost attribution, engagement-per-dollar (POSITIVE/NEUTRAL/NEGATIVE)
- **Product usage**: Pixel Agents runs, AmbientScore scans+paid, CardForge/StoryForge views

**Thresholds (RED = create finance task):**
Daily >1.5x budget ($0.75), waste >50%, cost/action >$0.05, weekly trend >30%

**Decision loop:** Audit → Analyze (RED/YELLOW/GREEN) → Optimize → Report
- Weekly financial reports (spec docs, check existing first)
- Meaningful memory saves (insights, not raw numbers)
- Cross-agent: Forge handles ops cost incidents, Cipher handles strategic analysis

**Key files:** `finance-intel.js` (digest + prompt block), `prompt-builders.js` (contract)

### Forge — Infrastructure Ops Director (Apr 2026)
Forge operates as a proactive infrastructure watchdog with a live Ops Intelligence Dashboard every heartbeat.

**Data (what Forge sees):**
- **Heartbeat health**: last 5 runs (status/duration/actions/blocks), failure rate, avg duration trend, per-agent reliability, top blocked patterns, backlog pressure
- **Cost monitor**: 7-day daily Gemini spend, avg/projected monthly, trend (rising/flat/falling), top 3 agent spenders, spike detection
- **Errors & performance**: p50/p95 latency, error counts by type from Application Insights
- **Governance**: 7-day violation count, per-agent breakdown, top violation type
- **Threshold alerts**: two-tier (YELLOW=monitor, RED=create ops_breakfix)

**Thresholds (RED = auto-create ops_breakfix):**
Heartbeat failure >40%, p95 >4000ms, errors >200/7d, cost >3x avg, backlog >95%

**Decision loop:** Assess → Triage (RED/YELLOW/GREEN) → Act (prioritized by blast radius)

**Stalled agent detection (Apr 2026):** ops-intel.js tracks `zeroActionRuns` per agent across recent heartbeat runs. If an agent produces 0 actions over 5+ consecutive runs (excluding Quill), a YELLOW alert fires in Forge's dashboard. Forge can then issue a system directive to course-correct the stalled agent.

**Human-like behaviors:**
- Incident learning: saves memories after ops_breakfix resolved (what → root cause → fix → prevention)
- Runbook creation: `create-doc (kind: runbook)` for issues occurring 3+ times
- Status communication: comments on Nova's highest-priority task during RED incidents
- Proactive maintenance: flags stale tasks, blocked agent patterns, governance trends
- **System directives:** can create `system_directive` tasks to course-correct broken agents (see Self-Correcting Agent System below)

**Key files:** `ops-intel.js` (digest + prompt block + stalled agent detection), `prompt-builders.js` (contract), `constants.js` (thresholds)

### Scribe — Content Director (Apr 2026)
Scribe upgraded from content executor to strategic content director. No new module — data already existed, just routed to Scribe's prompt.

**Voice direction (most important):** Write like a builder, not a marketer. CEO's north star: "The first thing you do in Blindspot is fight a stranger." Anti-patterns: "Introducing our latest...", emoji walls, feature dumps. "CEO EDIT FEEDBACK corrections ARE the style guide."

**5 prompt sections:** content performance (blog views + social engagement), campaign content status (behind/on-track), editor feedback patterns (Quill's recurring corrections), recent content (prevents topic repetition), content gaps (products without blog coverage 30d).

**Strategic contract:** Performance-driven writing, content pitching when idle (with objective_id), content repurposing before creating new, editor feedback loop.

### Pixel — Design Director (Apr 2026)
Pixel upgraded from hero image factory to design director. No new module.

**4 prompt sections:** visual performance (blog views + product page traffic), design queue (pending hero images), product visual identity + campaign asset status, design asset gaps (campaigns with 0 design tasks).

**Product-to-preset mapping:** Blindspot → ap-dark-cinematic/ap-dark-fantasy, AmbientOS → ap-neon-glass/ap-corporate-tech, CardForge → ap-fantasy-card/ap-ornate-frame, StoryForge → ap-watercolor/ap-dark-cinematic, Pixel Agents → ap-neon-glass/ap-holographic, AmbientScore → ap-corporate-tech/ap-gradient-mesh.

**Proactive design:** Creates tasks for campaigns missing visual assets. Prioritizes by product page traffic.

### Scout — Research Director (Apr 2026)
Scout upgraded from reactive researcher to strategic research director.

**New module:** `research-intel.js` — aggregates cross-agent demand signals into RESEARCH DEMAND DASHBOARD.

**Dashboard:** Demand signals (Echo declining platforms, Cipher negative ROI, Forge RED alerts), research requests from agent comments, prioritized backlog (scored by urgency+impact+freshness), competitive gaps per product (30-day window), research impact (citation rate).

**Competitive tracking standing orders:** per-product competitor landscapes. Cross-agent research requests via "Research request for Scout: [question]" in task comments.

### Self-Correcting Agent System (Apr 2026)
Agents can now course-correct each other without CEO intervention via **system directives**.

**How it works:**
1. Forge's Ops Dashboard detects a stalled/broken agent (0 output over 5+ runs, high block rate, or repeated failures)
2. Forge (or Nova) creates a `system_directive` task assigned to the broken agent:
   `{ "type": "create-task", "task": { "title": "DIRECTIVE: [instruction]", "description": "Diagnostic: [data]. Required: [fix].", "category": "system_directive", "assignee": "[agent-id]", "taskType": "ops" } }`
3. Target agent sees "SYSTEM DIRECTIVE — ACT ON THIS FIRST" prominently above their task list in the next heartbeat
4. Agent self-corrects by executing the directive. Anti-stall force-executes if ignored.
5. If directive goes unaddressed after 2 cycles, Forge escalates to Nova; Nova can escalate to CEO.

**Safety rails (server-side enforced in agent-runner.js):**
- Only `forge` and `nova` can create `system_directive` tasks (other agents blocked)
- Forge cannot directive Nova (must escalate to CEO)
- Max 1 active directive per target agent (prevents loops)
- Priority auto-set to `critical`
- Anti-stall sorts directives above all other idle tasks
- Quill excluded from stall detection (reactive editor)

**Key files:** `agent-runner.js` (authorization gate + anti-loop ceiling), `ops-intel.js` (stalled agent detection), `prompt-builders.js` (directive prompt injection + Forge/Nova instructions), `constants.js` (`DIRECTIVE_AUTHORIZED_AGENTS`, `OBJECTIVE_EXEMPT_CATEGORIES`)

### Shared Context Architecture (Apr 2026)
All AI-facing endpoints now share a common context module to prevent hallucination.

**Problem solved:** Standup, Nova Chat, Mood Engine, and Morning Report were generating AI output with minimal or zero company state, causing agents to hallucinate as if it were Day 1 of a new company.

**New shared modules:**
- `api/_utils/companyContextLoader.js` — options-gated data loader. Callers specify which state keys to load (tasks, campaigns, documents, memories, intel data, product facts). Parallel `storage.getState()` calls. Expensive loads (intel data = 11 keys) only when flagged.
- `api/_utils/companyContextFormatters.js` — 5 pure formatting functions that produce prompt text blocks:
  - `formatCoreContext(state, agentId)` — tasks w/ descriptions + comments, campaigns w/ briefs, objectives, recent accomplishments (48h). ~1000-1500 tokens. Used by: novachat, mood.
  - `formatRichContext(state, agentId)` — core + documents, memories, seed memories, product facts, site context. ~2000-2500 tokens. Used by: standup.
  - `formatIntelDigests(state)` — builds all 5 intel digests via existing heartbeat modules (social, ops, finance, research, performance). ~1500-2000 tokens. Used by: agentchat.
  - `formatMoodTelemetry(state)` — real task/campaign/heartbeat/cost counts. ~200-400 tokens. Used by: mood engine.
  - `formatMorningBrief(state)` — core + campaign descriptions + intel headlines + product summary. ~2000-2500 tokens. Used by: morning report.

**Context parity by endpoint:**
| Endpoint | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Standup (`company-standup-run`) | Task titles + campaign titles only | Full rich context (tasks, campaigns, docs, memories, products, accomplishments) |
| Nova Chat (`novachat`) | Zero company state | Core context in system instruction (both Gemini + Claude paths) |
| Mood Engine (`synthesizeNovaMood`) | 100% hardcoded fake telemetry | Real operational pulse (task counts, heartbeat health, cost trend) |
| Morning Report (`companyMorningReport`) | Aggregated counts only | Enriched with campaign descriptions, product facts, accomplishments |
| Agent Chat (`agentchat`) | Rich base context but no analysis | Intel digests for strategic agents (nova, cipher, forge, echo, scout) |

**Key design:** `formatCoreContext` includes a "RECENT ACCOMPLISHMENTS" section (tasks completed in last 48h with assignee). This is the primary hallucination killer — agents see real work has been done and can't pretend the platform is brand new.

**Intel module reuse:** Formatters import existing heartbeat digest builders directly (`social-intel.js`, `ops-intel.js`, `finance-intel.js`, `research-intel.js`, `performance-intel.js`). No duplication. Heartbeat's `prompt-builders.js` is untouched.

### Campaign Scheduler Task Assignment (Apr 2026)
The campaign auto-replenish scheduler (`index.js` ~line 305) maps task types to agents via `_taskTypeToAgent`:
- `blog_post` → **scribe** (was incorrectly mapped to echo, fixed Apr 2026)
- `social_linkedin`, `social_bluesky`, `social_x`, `social_facebook` → echo
- `design_asset` → pixel
- `research` → scout
- `internal_doc` → scribe
- `general` → nova
- `bluesky_discovery` → scout (Apr 2026, triggers Scout's inline discovery handler before Gemini call)
- `bluesky_reply` → scribe (Apr 2026, Scribe drafts reply → skips Quill → creates `social_post.reply` action → approval queue)

Note: agents **cannot reassign** already-assigned tasks via `update-task` (hard-blocked in task-mutations.js lines 312-318). Only Nova can assign unassigned tasks. If a task is created with the wrong assignee, it must be fixed via direct API call or CEO intervention.

### `escalated` Flag Warning
The `escalated` field on tasks means "requires CEO approval" (governance classification set at task creation for social tasks). It does NOT mean "stuck" or "blocked." The Task Board and Command Center do NOT use `escalated` for blocked counts — only `t.blocked` and `blocked` tag count.

### Pixel Agents Architecture
- 24 built-in agents across 12 categories
- Agent configs in TWO files (must stay in sync): `pixel-agents/data/pixel-agents.json` + `api/_data/pixel-agents.json`
- Agent capabilities: text-only, web search (Brave API), URL fetch, image generation (Gemini)
- API: 12 endpoints (`pixel-agent-*` + `agentforge-drafts`)
- Frontend calls Function App directly via `getApiBase()` — SWA proxy doesn't support POST
- Standalone minimal topbar navigation (no main site nav/footer)
- Stripe billing groundwork laid (not activated)
- See `.claude/skills/pixel-agents/SKILL.md` for full reference

### Agent Forge Pipeline
```
Build → Test → Submit → AI Gatekeeper Review → CEO Approval Queue → Live in Catalog
```
- Login required to build agents
- Drafts saved to blob storage (per-user, `agentforge-drafts` API)
- 3 submissions/day limit, 3 live agents cap
- AI gatekeeper scores quality/uniqueness/safety
- CEO approves via Content Hub or Actions page (unified queue)
- Agent lifecycle sidebar: Drafts / Pending / Live

---

## Model Configuration & Tuning (Apr 2026)

**Heartbeat AI model** is switchable via Azure env var `HEARTBEAT_MODEL`:
- `claude` — Claude Sonnet 4.6 (current, recommended). Better reasoning, reads dashboards, registers experiments, internalizes CEO style.
- `gemini` (or unset) — Gemini 2.0 Flash (cheaper, faster, but ignores complex prompt sections).

**Switch model:** Azure Portal → ambientpixels-nova-api → Environment variables → `HEARTBEAT_MODEL` = `claude` or `gemini`.

**Heartbeat interval:** `api/companyHeartbeat/function.json` → `schedule` field (NCRONTAB format). Currently `0 0 * * * *` (hourly). Was `0 */30 * * * *` (30 min) before Claude switch. Manual triggers via `/api/company-heartbeat-trigger` still work anytime.

**Cost:** Claude Sonnet at 1hr = ~$0.75/day. Gemini Flash at 30min = ~$0.50/day.

**All agent-facing systems use the same switch:**
- Heartbeat (8 agents) — `gemini.js`
- Agent Chat (sidebar quick-chat) — `agentchat/index.js`
- Nova Chat (full page) — `novachat/index.js`
- Morning Report — `companyMorningReport/index.js`
- Daily Standup — `company-standup-run/index.js`

**Chat system upgrades (Apr 2026):**
- Agent chat now loads full company context: all campaigns (with status, end dates, task counts, EXPIRED flags), all objectives (with status), agent memories, seed memories
- Nova has lifecycle actions in chat: pause-campaign, resume-campaign, complete-campaign, archive-objective, propose-campaign, propose-objective — executes directly, not just advises
- Structural JSON parser handles Claude's multiline responses (tables, pipes, emoji)
- Thinking indicator (animated dots) while agents respond
- Sidebar "Open full Agent Chat" link passes selected agent ID
- Basic markdown rendering in sidebar chat (bold, bullets, numbered lists, horizontal rules)

**Tuning lessons learned (Apr 2026):**
- Gemini 2.0 Flash ignores multi-section dashboard prompts — agents default to safe/familiar behavior. Required MANDATORY/FORBIDDEN nudges to get basic compliance.
- Claude Sonnet reads and reasons about dashboard data naturally — agents self-prioritize, register experiments, internalize CEO style without forced nudges.
- Stale agent memories create self-reinforcing loops (Cipher: "spend $0.51" 20x, Forge: "64KB limit" 20x). Fix: clear memories + FORBIDDEN instructions on generic saves.
- Seeding 2-3 CEO-directive tasks breaks agent inertia — gives agents concrete work to react to instead of waiting.
- Agent experiment system requires `experiment_tag` field in remember action — without it, memory is just a note, not a tracked experiment.
- **Orphan guard silently blocks operational agents.** Cipher and Forge were producing 0 actions for 10+ hours because the orphan guard blocked task creation without an objective_id. Fix: exempt finance, ops, ops_breakfix, governance, maintenance, system_directive categories.
- **Agents cannot reassign tasks.** task-mutations.js hard-blocks reassignment of already-assigned tasks. Nova was stuck in a 15+ cycle loop trying to reassign blog tasks from Echo to Scribe via update-task. The assignee field only accepts changes on unassigned tasks by Nova. Fix: correct the source (campaign scheduler's `_taskTypeToAgent` map).
- **Non-heartbeat endpoints hallucinate without context.** Standup, Nova Chat, Mood Engine, and Morning Report had minimal/zero company state in their prompts. Agents generated "Day 1" fiction despite 48 CSS files, active campaigns, and published blogs existing. Fix: shared context modules (`companyContextLoader.js` + `companyContextFormatters.js`) provide grounded state to all AI endpoints.
- **ops-intel.js format mismatch.** Forge's per-agent reliability section was reading `r.agentResults` (old format) while heartbeat runs now use `r.perAgent`. Result: Forge was blind to all agent-level health data. Always verify data format assumptions when reading heartbeat run records.

---

## Critical Safety Rules

1. **High blast radius files** — do NOT edit without explicit user request:
   - `api/companyHeartbeat/index.js`, `api/company-state/index.js`, `staticwebapp.config.json`
   - `data/company-actions.json`, CI/CD workflow, `governance.html`, `local.settings.json`
2. **Never clear these state keys** without explicit request: `documents`, `agentMemories`, `researchIntel`, `runtimeMemory`, `heartbeatRuns`, `governanceLog`, `agentSeedMemories`, `agentConfigs`
3. **Git repo is at `ambientpixels/.git`** — NOT the parent `Ambientpixels/` directory
4. **OneDrive can corrupt `.git`** — if git fails, check `ambientpixels/.git` exists first
5. **Python not available** on this Windows machine — use Node.js for scripting
6. **`MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`** required for Azure CLI paths in Git Bash
7. **NEVER use `az functionapp deployment source config-zip`** — manual zip deploy corrupts the Function App deployment state (`WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE` gets set to a blob URL, breaking GitHub Actions deploys). Always deploy via `git push origin master` → GitHub Actions. If the Function App is broken, delete `WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE` app setting and stop/start.
8. **Azure Function App caches old code aggressively** — Consumption plan workers can serve stale code even after a successful GitHub Actions deploy. A restart may not help. Known issue (Apr 2026). Workaround: stop + start (not just restart), or check Azure Portal Deployment Center for sync options.
9. **Social platform credentials live in Azure env vars, NOT state keys.** Bluesky uses `BLUESKY_HANDLE` + `BLUESKY_APP_PASSWORD` (see `actionsExecute/executors/social/bluesky.js:16-21`). Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Reddit follow the same pattern — each has its own env vars. Do NOT confuse with `socialAccountStats` (analytics/follower counts) or `socialCredentials` state key. If a new social integration is added, set the env vars in Azure Portal, not in blob state.

---

## Model Configuration & Runtime Switching (Apr 2026)

**Heartbeat AI model** is now switchable at runtime via the `systemConfig` state key — no redeploy or Azure Portal access needed.

**Backend (`api/companyHeartbeat/gemini.js`):**
- Reads `systemConfig.heartbeatModel` from Azure Blob (5-min cache)
- Falls back to `HEARTBEAT_MODEL` env var if systemConfig not set
- Supported values: `claude-sonnet` (Claude Sonnet 4.6), `claude-haiku` (Claude Haiku 4.5), `gemini` (Gemini 2.0 Flash)
- Model resolved dynamically on every `callGemini()` / `callGeminiExecute()` call

**Dashboard (Dev View → AI Model Fleet panel):**
- Pill toggle buttons: click to switch between Sonnet / Haiku / Gemini Flash
- Saves to `systemConfig.heartbeatModel` immediately
- Fleet list shows "HEARTBEAT" + "PRIMARY" badge on active model
- CEO status strip shows active model name

**Cost comparison:**
| Model | Input | Output | Best for |
|-------|-------|--------|----------|
| Claude Sonnet 4.6 | $3.00/1M | $15.00/1M | Full reasoning, dashboard analysis, experiment tracking |
| Claude Haiku 4.5 | $0.80/1M | $4.00/1M | Good reasoning at ~4x less cost than Sonnet |
| Gemini 2.0 Flash | $0.10/1M | $0.40/1M | Cheapest, but ignores complex multi-section prompts |

**All agent-facing systems use the same switch:** heartbeat, agent chat, Nova chat, standup, morning report, daily standup.

---

## Removed Systems (Apr 2026 Cleanup)

The following client-side browser systems were removed as dead weight — all were disabled by default, never auto-triggered, and redundant with the server-side heartbeat:

| System | What it was | Why removed |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| **Worker Framework** | Client-side browser workers that monitored dashboard pressure | Redundant — Nova sees all tasks via heartbeat |
| **Planner Loop** | Weekly deterministic planning proposals | Never invoked, disabled by default |
| **Calibration Loop** | Weekly self-improvement proposals | Never invoked, disabled by default |
| **Priority Engine** | Client-side task scoring | Never called (`recalculateAll` had zero callers) |
| **ActionRouter** | Client-side action execution pipeline | Disabled by default, never triggered |
| **ActionExecutors** | Execute approved planner/calibration actions | Dead — planner/calibration removed |
| **ActionQueue** | Client-side pending action queue | Dead — no system writes to it |

**47 files deleted, ~8,300 lines removed.** Config panel simplified: Worker/Planner/Calibration panels removed, "Kill All Automation" button removed, Action Router panel replaced with "Agent Modes" (just Activation Mode + Automation Mode selectors).

**Tasks page:** Priority pills now use `task.priority` directly instead of the deleted PriorityEngine.

### Campaign Task Due Dates (Apr 2026)
Campaign auto-replenish (`index.js` ~line 363) now sets default `dueDate` based on campaign cadence:
- `daily` → 1 day
- `weekly` → 3 days
- `biweekly` → 5 days
- fallback → 3 days

Previously campaign tasks had no due dates and would float forever.

### Research Brief Visibility (Apr 2026)
Trend radar auto-briefs are now created as `todo` (was `backlog`). Scout can see and work on them immediately — previously only Nova could triage backlog tasks.

---

## Reference Files

For deep dives, read these files in the `references/` directory:

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `agents.md` | All 8 agents: roles, tiers, doctrine, capabilities, automations, special behaviors |
| `heartbeat.md` | Heartbeat execution flow, prompt layers, module details, error handling |
| `pipelines.md` | Social/blog/wiki pipelines, task status lifecycle, copy propagation |
| `api.md` | All 88 endpoints, 43 state keys, auth mechanism, storage layer, demo guard |
| `governance.md` | Guardrails, proposal gates, execution modes, safety architecture, audit trails |
| `architecture.md` | CSS system, theme tokens, deployment pipeline, dependencies, file inventory |

# AmbientScore Development Skill

AmbientScore is AmbientPixels' standalone AI website conversion audit product. Users enter a URL, get an instant 0-100 score with a letter grade, see 3 teaser findings for free, and can unlock the full report ($49 single / $149 3-pack). The product lives at `/ambientscore/` and is self-contained — its own CSS, JS, and API layer.

## Recent Changes

_Changelog maintained by CEO. Agents should read this first — it reflects the most recent state of AmbientScore and may contradict older sections below. The sync script pulls this section to the top of every injected skill block. Entries older than 30 days get condensed into the main skill body._

_No recent entries. CEO: add dated bullet points here as AmbientScore evolves (scoring model changes, new dimensions, pricing tweaks, report layout updates, credit pack changes, etc.)._

## Architecture Overview

### Frontend Pages

| Page | File | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| Landing | `ambientscore/index.html` + `js/ambientscore.js` | URL input, free scan results, upgrade CTA |
| Report | `ambientscore/report.html` + `js/report.js` | Full report viewer with paywall logic |
| Strategy | `ambientscore/strategy.html` + `js/strategy.js` | Lead capture intake form |
| Confirm | `ambientscore/confirm.html` | Slot booking confirmation |

### API Endpoints

| Endpoint | Method | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `/api/as-analyze` | POST | Core scan — accepts `{ url }` or `{ sessionId }` (payment verification) |
| `/api/as-report` | GET | Report retrieval — `?id=<reportId>`, returns teaser or full based on unlock status |
| `/api/as-credits` | POST | Credit check (`action: "check"`) or redemption (`action: "redeem"`) |
| `/api/as-confirm` | POST | Strategy session confirmation with HMAC validation |
| `/api/formIntake` | POST | Shared intake — type `"ambientscore_strategy"` for strategy submissions |

### Library Modules (`api/_lib/ambientScore/`)

| Module | Role |
|--------|------|
| `analyzer.js` | Pipeline orchestrator — scrape → extract → classify → evaluate → score → synthesize |
| `scraper.js` | URL fetching with SSRF protection, cheerio HTML parsing |
| `dimensions.js` | 8-dimension model definition, weight profiles by site type, scoring helpers |
| `promptBuilder.js` | Gemini prompt templates for each pipeline stage |
| `scorer.js` | Deterministic scoring — decompression curve (1→0, 5→60, 10→100) |
| `reportRenderer.js` | HTML report template generation |
| `creditUtils.js` | Pack credit ledger (purchase/redeem history per email hash) |
| `stripeClient.js` | Stripe checkout creation, session verification, webhook signatures |
| `emailSender.js` | Azure Communication Services email delivery |

## The 8-Dimension Scoring Model

The scoring model is the intellectual core of the product. It lives in `dimensions.js` and drives everything from prompt construction to report rendering.

### Group A — Conversion Funnel (55% base weight)

1. **Messaging Clarity** (15%) — Headline clarity, value prop specificity, jargon avoidance, consistency
2. **CTA Strength** (15%) — Visibility, action language, value alignment, placement
3. **Funnel Friction** (15%) — Step count, cognitive load, form optimization, distractions
4. **Conversion Hierarchy** (10%) — Visual hierarchy, information flow, progressive disclosure

### Group B — Trust & Differentiation (45% base weight)

5. **Trust Signals** (15%) — Social proof quality, authority markers, risk reversal, transparency
6. **Differentiation** (10%) — Unique mechanism, competitor contrast, category ownership
7. **Audience Alignment** (10%) — Language match, pain point addressing, sophistication calibration
8. **Quick-Win Fixes** (10%) — Low-hanging fruit count, implementation ease

Each dimension has 3-4 sub-criteria. Gemini scores each sub-criterion 1-10, then the decompression curve maps LLM scores to 0-100 (because LLMs compress scores toward 5-7, a raw 5 maps to 60, not 50). Weights are dynamic — `dimensions.js` has profiles for SaaS, enterprise, ecommerce, content, media, local service, and agency site types.

### When modifying the scoring model

- Adding a dimension: update `dimensions.js` (definition + weights for ALL site-type profiles), `promptBuilder.js` (evaluation prompts for the correct group), `scorer.js` (if weight math changes), and `reportRenderer.js` (display).
- Changing weights: only touch `dimensions.js`. The scorer reads weights from there.
- Changing the decompression curve: only touch `scorer.js`. The curve parameters are there.

## Analysis Pipeline (4 Stages)

The pipeline in `analyzer.js` runs 4 Gemini calls (2 in parallel for Group A/B evaluation):

**Stage 0 — Scraping** (`scraper.js`): Fetch URL, parse HTML with cheerio, extract headings, CTAs, forms, social proof, pricing, schema.org, body text. SSRF protection blocks localhost, private IPs, and cloud metadata endpoints.

**Stage 1 — Extraction** (Gemini call #1): Parse scraped data into structured JSON — headlines, value props, CTAs, trust elements, audience signals, friction points, conversion paths.

**Stage 1.5 — Classification** (Gemini call #2): Classify site type (SaaS, enterprise, ecommerce, etc.) to select the right weight profile.

**Stage 2 — Evaluation** (2 parallel Gemini calls): Group A and Group B dimensions each get their own call. Returns 1-10 scores per sub-criterion + reasoning + findings.

**Stage 3 — Scoring & Synthesis** (`scorer.js`): Apply decompression curve, compute weighted score, generate priorities, headline/CTA rewrites, confidence level.

### Pipeline development rules

- Gemini prompts live in `promptBuilder.js` — keep prompt changes isolated there, not in `analyzer.js`.
- The analyzer orchestrates; it should not contain prompt text or scoring logic.
- Rate limiting (5 free scans/hour per IP) is enforced in `as-analyze/index.js`, not in the library.
- Report data is stored as `cc_report_<reportId>` in Azure Blob via `company-state` API.

## Monetization & Credits

### Stripe Flow

1. User clicks "Unlock" → `ambientscore.js` calls `/api/as-analyze` with just `{ url }` initially for free scan
2. For paid unlock → Stripe Checkout session created in `as-analyze/index.js` via `stripeClient.js`
3. After payment → redirect back with `sessionId` → `as-analyze` verifies payment and unlocks report
4. 3-pack purchase: 1 credit auto-redeemed for triggering report, 2 remaining

### Credit Ledger

- Storage key: `cc_credits_<emailHash>` in Azure Blob
- `creditUtils.js` manages the ledger: purchase entries, redeem entries, balance calculation
- Credits are checked/redeemed via `/api/as-credits` endpoint
- Frontend stores credit state in `sessionStorage` under `cc_pack_credits`

## CSS Conventions

- **Prefix**: `as-*` for all classes (e.g., `as-score-gauge`, `as-finding-card`, `as-hero`)
- **Self-contained**: `ambientscore.css` has no dependencies on the AmbientPixels framework
- **Design tokens**: `--as-bg`, `--as-surface`, `--as-accent` (emerald green `#10b981`), `--as-text`, `--as-muted`
- **Responsive**: Desktop-first, breakpoints at 768px and 480px
- **Print styles**: Hidden CTAs/upgrades, white background — reports are designed to be printable
- Search `ambientscore.css` before creating new classes — reuse what exists

## JavaScript Conventions

- **Pattern**: IIFE (Immediately Invoked Function Expressions) — no module bundler, no framework
- **DOM**: Vanilla `document.querySelector` / `innerHTML` — no jQuery, no React
- **Security**: All user-facing strings go through `escapeHtml()` utility
- **State**: Module-scoped variables (`currentReportId`, `currentUrl`) — no global state
- **Error handling**: User-friendly inline error messages, not console-only

## Storage Keys

| Key Pattern | Contents |
|-------------|----------|
| `cc_report_<reportId>` | Full report JSON (score, dimensions, findings, rewrites) |
| `cc_ratelimit` | IP-based rate limit tracking |
| `cc_analytics` | Scan event analytics (90-day retention, 10K cap) |
| `cc_credits_<emailHash>` | Credit purchase/redeem ledger |

These use the `company-state` API with `x-company-secret: pixelpusher` header. The `cc_` prefix is a legacy from ConversionCore — do not rename (backward compat).

## Email Integration

- Provider: Azure Communication Services (ACS)
- Sender: `DoNotReply@ambientpixels.ai`
- Template in `emailSender.js` — self-contained HTML safe for all email clients
- Triggered after report unlock — sends full report summary to purchaser's email

## Security Considerations

- **SSRF**: `scraper.js` blocks private IPs, localhost, and cloud metadata URLs before fetching
- **Rate limiting**: 5 free scans/hour per IP in `as-analyze/index.js`
- **HMAC**: Strategy confirmation uses HMAC token validation
- **Anti-spam**: Form intake has honeypot field, minimum time-to-submit (2.5s), rate limiting
- **Stripe webhooks**: Signature verification in `stripeClient.js`
- Never bypass these protections — if they're in the way during development, ask the user

## Common Development Tasks

### Adding a new dimension
1. Define in `dimensions.js`: name, description, sub-criteria, weight in ALL site-type profiles
2. Add evaluation prompt in `promptBuilder.js` (assign to Group A or B)
3. Update `reportRenderer.js` to display the new dimension
4. Verify `scorer.js` picks it up (it reads from `dimensions.js` dynamically)

### Modifying report output
- Report HTML template: `reportRenderer.js`
- Report viewer (frontend): `report.html` + `report.js`
- Report data structure: created in `analyzer.js` Stage 3

### Changing pricing
- Stripe prices are configured in `stripeClient.js` (price IDs)
- Display prices in `ambientscore.js` (landing page CTAs) and `report.js` (paywall section)
- Credit pack size in `creditUtils.js`

### Adding a new API endpoint
- Create `api/as-<name>/index.js` + `function.json`
- Add route in `staticwebapp.config.json` if needed (but be careful — that file has high blast radius)
- Follow existing patterns: `x-company-secret` header check, try/catch with 500 response, JSON body parsing

## Future: Claude Migration

There's a standing plan to switch from Gemini to Claude API for the analysis pipeline (better reasoning, more nuanced observations). Not yet active — the user said "not now." When AmbientScore analysis quality comes up, this option is worth mentioning.

# Blindspot Game — Development Skill

Use this skill when working on the Blindspot game — a standalone arena combat game at `/blindspot/`. Blindspot is fully independent from CardForge as of Mar 21, 2026 — zero shared CSS, JS, images, or audio. APIs forked but card save remains shared (product-agnostic).

## Recent Changes

_Changelog maintained by CEO. Agents should read this first — it reflects the most recent state of Blindspot and may contradict older sections below. The sync script pulls this section to the top of every injected skill block. Entries older than 30 days get condensed into the main skill body._

_No recent entries. CEO: add dated bullet points here as Blindspot evolves (new mechanics, balance changes, campaign releases, PvP tuning, etc.)._

## Iteration Cycle (MANDATORY)

Every change MUST follow this cycle:

1. **Read what the user is asking** — understand the actual problem
2. **Understand from the player's perspective** — what does the player see/feel?
3. **Design the solution** — plan before coding
4. **Build it**
5. **Parse check** — `node -e "new Function(require('fs').readFileSync('file','utf8'))"`
6. **Smoke test** — `node ambientpixels/blindspot/tests/smoke-test.js`
7. **Commit + push**
8. **Ask: did this solve what the user actually wanted?**

## Current State (~120 iterations, Mar 2026)

### File Structure
```
ambientpixels/blindspot/
├── index.html              — Landing page + Stranger fight + Quick Build + New Card flow
├── play.html               — Lobby, Campaign, PvP, Battle screens (loading gate)
├── login.html              — Blindspot-themed pre-login page
├── js/
│   ├── blindspot-flow.js   — Game logic (~6200 lines, monolith split complete)
│   ├── blindspot-quick-build.js — Quick Build wizard (~700 lines, uses BlindspotSaveCard)
│   └── lib/                — Modules (extracted from monolith + forked from CardForge)
│       ├── bs-constants.js     — All game constants (window.BsConst)
│       ├── bs-state.js         — Progression, server sync, safeLSSet (window.BsState)
│       ├── bs-audio-sfx.js     — Web Audio synth SFX + battle ambient (window.BsSfx)
│       ├── bs-toast.js         — Toast notifications (window.BsToast)
│       ├── bs-cosmetics.js     — Cosmetic inventory, equip, collection UI (window.BsCosmetics)
│       ├── bs-crates.js        — Crate inventory, loot roll, opening ceremony (window.BsCrates)
│       ├── bs-strategy.js      — Passives, archetypes, prefight info (window.BsStrategy)
│       ├── bs-card-renderer.js — Card HTML renderer + stat migration (window.BsCardRenderer)
│       ├── bs-config.js        — API endpoints (blindspotbattle, blindspotbosses, shared savecards)
│       ├── bs-csrf.js          — CSRF token injection
│       ├── bs-utils.js         — Minimal escapeHtml, isValidUrl, sanitizeString
│       ├── bs-stubs.js         — EffectTiers + Entitlements stubs
│       ├── bs-arena-api.js     — ArenaAPI (points to Blindspot endpoints)
│       ├── bs-arena-audio.js   — SFX + music (uses /blindspot/audio/)
│       ├── bs-arena-battle-ui.js — Battle screen rendering
│       ├── bs-arena-results.js — Post-battle results
│       ├── bs-arena-backgrounds.js — Arena picker (uses /blindspot/img/arena/)
│       ├── bs-arena-card-select.js — Card picker + stat mapping
│       ├── bs-ai.js            — Gemini AI wrapper for Quick Build
│       ├── bs-presets.js       — Card preset templates
│       ├── bs-save-card.js     — Direct card save (replaces CardForge editor pipeline)
│       ├── bs-card-share.js   — Canvas→PNG card renderer + download/clipboard share modal
│       ├── bs-pvp.js          — Async PvP: 3-tab UI (Challenge, Defense, Inbox) (window.BsPvp)
│       └── bs-adventure.js    — CYOA pre-boss adventure engine (~500 lines)
├── css/
│   ├── blindspot.css       — Full visual identity (~7400 lines)
│   └── blindspot-cards.css — Quick Build qb-* base styles (forked, themed with --bs-* tokens)
├── data/
│   ├── stranger-card.json  — The Stranger card (Fighter, 285 pts)
│   ├── bosses.json         — 10 campaign + 4 weekly boss configs with rewards
│   ├── game-config.json    — Tunable config (crate types, loot tables, drop pools)
│   ├── prefill-card.json   — Empty (prevents 404)
│   └── adventures/         — CYOA pre-boss adventure data
│       ├── manifest.json       — Registry of which bosses have adventures
│       ├── bs-boss-1.json      — The Gate (Gatekeeper adventure)
│       ├── bs-boss-2.json      — The Warden's Corridor
│       ├── bs-boss-3.json      — The Haunted Ward
│       ├── bs-boss-4.json      — The Server Room
│       ├── bs-boss-5.json      — The Mountain Pass
│       ├── bs-boss-6.json      — The Library of Leech
│       ├── bs-boss-7.json      — The Iron Bastion
│       ├── bs-boss-8.json      — The House of Mirrors
│       ├── bs-boss-9.json      — The Killing Floor
│       └── bs-boss-10.json     — The Forge Eternal
├── img/
│   ├── arena/              — 6 arena stage backgrounds (.webp)
│   ├── bosses/             — 10 boss character images (.webp)
│   └── demo/               — 3 demo character images (.webp)
├── audio/                  — 23 SFX + music files (20 forked + 3 adventure ambient)
├── image-manifest.json     — Gallery image manifest for Quick Build
├── image-manifest-thumbs.json — Thumbnail manifest
├── tests/
│   └── smoke-test.js       — 23-check validation (parse, CSS, HTML, bosses)
├── b2c-template.html       — Azure B2C login template (uploaded to blob storage)
├── b2c-custom.css          — Blindspot B2C branding CSS
└── b2c-default.css         — Neutral dark B2C branding CSS (tenant default)
```

### Server Files (Blindspot-Owned)
- `api/blindspotbattle/index.js` — Blindspot battle engine (forked from CardForge, Blindspot progression only)
- `api/blindspotbattle/arena-bosses.json` — 10 Blindspot bosses + 4 weekly (no CardForge bosses)
- `api/blindspotbosses/index.js` — Boss data endpoint (Blindspot bosses only)
- `api/blindspotbosses/arena-bosses.json` — Same filtered boss list
- `api/blindspotasyncbattle/index.js` — Async PvP battle engine (defender AI, full combat simulation, Elo + Sparks payout)
- `api/blindspotdefensequeue/index.js` — Global defense queue (register/withdraw/list, 1 card per user, auto-prune 7 days)
- `api/blindspotresultsinbox/index.js` — Per-user async PvP results inbox (fetch/dismiss/dismissAll/clear)
- `api/blindspotprofile/index.js` — Blindspot player profile (Elo, record, defenseCardId, progression)
- `api/cardforgesavecards/index.js` — Card save API (shared, product-agnostic)
- `staticwebapp.config.json` — `/blindspot/*` route, `/api/blindspotbattle`, `/api/blindspotbosses`, `/api/blindspotasyncbattle`, `/api/blindspotdefensequeue`, `/api/blindspotresultsinbox` rewrites

### Critical Integration Gotchas
1. **THREE boss files must stay in sync**: `api/blindspotbattle/arena-bosses.json`, `api/blindspotbosses/arena-bosses.json`, AND `blindspot/data/bosses.json` (client-side)
2. **Auth on play.html**: `updatePlayAuthUI()` checks `/.auth/me` directly and sets `sessionStorage.isAuthenticated` — needed for CardForge save pipeline
3. **`handleSaveCard()` fetch is fire-and-forget** (not awaited) — need 3s+ wait after save
4. **`isNewPlayer()` checks localStorage `blindspot-onboarded` flag + server profile** (selectedCardId, xp, wins) — survives browser clears
5. **Server reads `card.class`** not `characterClass` for ability assignment
6. **Boss data has server-side cache** (`_bossCache`) — new bosses need cold restart
7. **All battle starts send `cardData` as fallback** — prevents "Card not found" when server save was delayed
8. **Returning authenticated players auto-redirect** from index.html to play.html — `!isDemo() && !isNewPlayer(profile)` check
9. **CSS overlays**: `bs-overlay--hidden` uses `display: none !important` — never create CSS rules that set display on overlay containers
10. **localStorage is fragile**: ALL writes go through `safeLSSet()` helper (top of blindspot-flow.js) which catches QuotaExceededError, clears expendable caches, and retries. NEVER use raw `localStorage.setItem()`.
11. **Quick Build class selectors**: Template renders `bs-stat-row` and `bs-stats-budget` (NOT `qb-stat-row` / `qb-stats-budget`). JS queries must match.
12. **Card save creates NEW cards**: Blindspot pages have no `card-id` hidden input, so `handleSaveCard()` always generates a new ID. Old cards persist on server.
13. **initPlay() has top-level try/catch**: If anything crashes, loading gate is dismissed. Never let errors leave the gate stuck.
14. **Card container type stored in 3 locations**: `card.design.imageContainer` (CardForge save), `card.imageContainer` (Blindspot Forge save), `card.cardData.design.imageContainer` (server nested). Renderer checks all three.
15. **Deck view forces fullbleed**: `renderDeckManagement()` overrides `imageContainer` to `'fullbleed'` for consistent grid display.
16. **Deck card selection is in-place**: Clicking a card in deck view swaps active state via DOM manipulation (not grid re-render) to avoid image flash/reload.

### The Player Flow
```
Landing (index.html):
  New player → Fight → Stranger Intro → Stranger Fight → Win/Loss
    → Win → Boss 1 auto-beaten (localStorage: bs-highest-boss=1) → Quick Build (5-step) → Card Reveal → play.html
    → [demo] Sign-in prompt after Quick Build
  Returning auth player → auto-redirect to play.html (no landing page flash)
  New Card flow → ?newCard=true param → Quick Build → save → play.html

Play (play.html):
  Loading gate → profile + card load → dismiss gate → Lobby
  Lobby → Fight Next Boss (quick-fight) OR Campaign (browse ladder)
  Lobby → Card switcher (arrows to cycle owned cards) + New Card button
  Campaign → Pre-fight overlay (boss info + weakness) → Battle → Loot Choice → [Forge trigger if ready]
  Forge → Stats tab / Look tab (palettes + containers via Sparks) / Details tab (name, quote, avatar gallery + AI gen)
  PvP → 3 sub-tabs (unlocked after Boss 10):
    Challenge → Defense queue browser (Elo-sorted) + Gallery PvP → Async Battle
    Defense → Register/withdraw a card for others to challenge (1 per user)
    Inbox → Results (wins/losses while offline) + Revenge buttons + passive Sparks earned
```

### Combat System (Server-Side)
- **Moves:** Strike, Guard, Ability, Heal, Counter (rock-paper-scissors interactions)
- **Stat-threshold passives** (computed server-side in `computeStatThresholdPassives()`):
  - STR 60+: Heavy Hitter (guard pierce 20%) | STR 80+: Brutal (+25% crit damage)
  - AGI 60+: Quick Draw (speed priority) | AGI 80+: Elusive (15% dodge)
  - INT 60+: Focused (ability costs 1 charge + 1 less stamina) | INT 80+: Arcane Mastery (+30% ability dmg)
  - END 60+: Resilient (heal grants 10% DR) | END 80+: Unbreakable (auto-heal 5 HP/round)
  - LCK 50+: Fortune (+10% crit chance) | LCK 70+: Wild Card (crits deal 2x)
- **Boss weakness exploit**: Player deals bonus damage (10-25%) when their stat matches boss weakness
- **Move upgrades**: Buttons rename at stat thresholds (Strike → Heavy Strike, etc.)
- **Archetypes**: Berserker (STR+LCK), Tank (END+AGI), Mage (INT+AGI), Assassin (AGI+STR), Gambler (LCK+INT)
- **Move combos** (server-validated, `handleMove()` in `blindspotbattle/index.js`):
  - **Flurry**: Strike → Strike → Strike = +30% damage on 3rd strike
  - **Riposte**: Guard → Counter = forced reflect (even if opponent didn't strike), or +25% bonus on natural reflect
  - **Empowered**: Heal → Ability = +50% ability damage
  - Detected from `player.moves` array history. Returns `comboTriggered` in roundResult.
- **Combat feedback** (client-side, `bs-arena-battle-ui.js`):
  - Matchup banners: green "Strike disrupts Heal!" / red "Strike blocked by Guard!" based on `MOVE_BEATS`
  - Passive activation flashes: detect from server events, show named flash under player card
  - Combo banners: big animated name + icon when combo triggers
  - Combo hints: amber glow + "COMBO" badge on move button when 1 move away from triggering
- **HP formula** (server-side, all 3 battle engines): `60 + (END × 5) + (STR × 1)` — range ~110-175 for bosses
- **Strike damage** (server-side): `STR × 0.5 + rand(STR × 0.15)` — ~50-65% of STR per hit
- **Heal** (server-side): `END × 0.35 + rand(END × 0.08)` — ~35-43% of END per heal
- **Stamina system** (server-side, `blindspotbattle/index.js`; config in `arena-config.json`):
  - Pool: `14 + floor(END × 0.5)` — range 14-23. Auto-regen: `1 + floor(END / 10)` per round (1-2)
  - Costs: Strike 4, Guard 1, Heal 2, Counter 4, Ability 5
  - Exhaustion: below 5 stamina → 6% maxHP burn per round (accelerates endgame, doesn't reduce damage)
  - Stat hooks: AGI 60+ (Quick Draw) reduces first move cost by 1, INT 60+ reduces Ability cost by 1, LCK crit refunds 1 stamina (both sides). Discounts stack (AGI+INT = Ability costs 3).
  - Enforcement: Ability hard-blocked if stamina < cost. All other moves always available (soft HP burn penalty).
  - Boss AI: stamina-aware — reduces weight for expensive moves when low, boosts Guard below 25% stamina.
  - Client: purple stamina bar under HP bar (both sides), cost badges (⚡N) on move buttons, exhaustion pulse animation.
  - Constants: `BsConst.STAMINA_COSTS`, `BsConst.STAMINA_EXHAUSTION_THRESHOLD`
  - Tunable: all values in `arena-config.json` → `staminaConfig`
- **Cooldown system** (server-side, `blindspotbattle/index.js`; config in `arena-config.json`):
  - Strike: 0, Guard: 0, Heal: 1-round CD, Counter: 1-round CD, Ability: 2-round CD
  - Server hard-blocks moves on cooldown. Boss AI zeroes weight for moves on CD.
  - Client: conic-gradient clock overlay (`::before`) covers entire button — dark pie shrinks clockwise revealing button. Countdown number in center. Purple ready-pulse when CD clears.
  - `updateCooldownOverlays(cds)` in `bs-arena-battle-ui.js` — sets `--cd-deg` CSS var + `data-cd` attribute + `--on-cooldown` class (pointer-events: none).
  - Combo compatibility: Flurry (Strike×3) unaffected. Riposte (Guard→Counter) works (Guard no CD). Empowered (Heal→Ability) works (Heal first, Ability next round).
  - Cooldown state: `battle.cooldowns = { player: {}, opponent: {} }` — keys are move names, values are remaining rounds. Decrement-then-set ordering each round.
  - Constants: `BsConst.COOLDOWN_ROUNDS`
  - Tunable: `arena-config.json` → `cooldownConfig`
- **Stance system** (server-side, `blindspotbattle/index.js`; config in `arena-config.json`):
  - 3 stances: Aggressive (+25% dmg, take 20% more, +1 stamina cost, +15% crit), Defensive (-20% dmg, Guard 80%, Heal +30%, -1 stamina cost, burn halved), Balanced (default)
  - Switch cost: 2 stamina (Balanced free). One switch per round, before move.
  - Boss HP threshold shifts: Aggressive >60%, Defensive 30-60%, Desperate (Aggressive) <30%. Computed each round from `opponent.hp / opponent.maxHp`.
  - Server: `battle.stances = { player: 'balanced', opponent: 'balanced' }`. Whitelist validation. Switch cost deducted before move resolves (intentional — risky all-in).
  - `resolveRound` applies: dmgMult (outgoing), defMult (incoming — Aggressive ×1.2 taken), guardBlock override (Defensive 0.8), healMult (Defensive ×1.3), critBonus (Aggressive +0.15), burnMult (Defensive ×0.5).
  - Multipliers compound intentionally: both Aggressive = ×1.25 × ×1.2 = ×1.5 total damage.
  - Stamina cost adj: Aggressive +1, Defensive -1 (min 1). Applied after AGI/INT discounts.
  - Boss AI: Defensive boosts guard/heal +10, Aggressive boosts strike +10/ability +5.
  - Client: 3 circular buttons above moves (fire=red, shield=blue, nodes=amber). `_playerStance` tracked in module state, sent as `stance` in move payload. `updateBossStance(stance)` updates opponent nameplate badge + shift log entry.
  - Tutorial: speech bubble step for `#arena-stance-row` in `TUTORIAL_STEPS`.
  - Constants: `BsConst.STANCE_DEFS`
  - Tunable: `arena-config.json` → `stanceConfig`
- **Per-card battle history** (server-side, `profile.cardHistory[cardId]`):
  - Tracked: wins, losses, bossesBeaten[], bestStreak, currentStreak, nemesis, nemesisLosses{}
  - Returned in `battleResult.cardHistory` after each fight
  - Client stores in `_progress.cardHistory`, displays in lobby HUD
- **Border evolution** (6 tiers, CSS `data-border-tier` attribute):
  - plain (0 wins) → bronze (5) → silver (15) → gold (30) → platinum (50) → radiant (100, animated glow)
  - Defined in `BsConst.BORDER_TIERS`, computed in `BsCardRenderer.getCardBorderTier()`
- **Card title milestones** (9 milestones in `BsConst.CARD_TITLE_MILESTONES`):
  - Blooded (1W), Proven (10W), Veteran (25W), Champion (50W), Legend (100W)
  - Hot Streak (5 best), Unstoppable (10 best), Boss Slayer (5 bosses), Conqueror (10 bosses)
  - Auto-applied to card renderer when no cosmetic title equipped

### Async PvP System (Phase 21 — implemented Mar 24, 2026)

**Architecture:**
- 3 Azure Functions: `blindspotdefensequeue`, `blindspotasyncbattle`, `blindspotresultsinbox`
- Defense queue: global blob `blindspot/defenseQueue.json`, 1 card per user, max 500 entries, auto-prune 7 days
- Async battle: attacker plays real-time vs AI-controlled defender card. Battle IDs prefixed `bs-async-`
- Results inbox: per-user blob `blindspot/asyncResults/{userId}.json`, max 50 entries, dismiss/dismissAll/clear

**Defender AI (`generateDefenderMove`):**
- 12 class-specific weight profiles (Fighter, Enforcer, Berserker, Guardian, Caster, Scholar, Hacker, Scout, Rogue, Trickster, Medic, Pilot)
- Reactive: low HP (<30%) → +25 heal/+15 guard weight; <50% → +10 heal/+5 guard
- Pattern reading: 2x attacker strike → +20 counter/+10 guard; attacker healed last round → +15 strike/+10 ability
- Charge-aware: redistributes ability weight to strike when charges < ability cost

**Elo & Sparks:**
- Attacker K-factor: 32, Defender K-factor: 16 (halved — didn't choose the fight)
- Win: 20 base + up to 15 bonus (Elo gap / 50), Loss: 5 consolation
- Revenge: +50% Sparks bonus on win
- Defender: +2 passive Sparks per battle received (win or lose)
- Anti-farming: 2hr cooldown per defender (`lastChallengedBy` + `lastChallengedAt` on queue entry)

**Client Integration:**
- PvP screen 3 sub-tabs: Challenge, Defense, Inbox — `bs-pvp.js` manages all three via `initPvPTabs()` + `[data-pvp-tab]` attributes
- `bs-arena-api.js`: auto-routes `submitMove`/`forfeit` to async endpoint when `battleId.startsWith('bs-async-')`
- `bs-pvp.js` (`window.BsPvp`): full UI module — `renderDefenseQueue()`, `renderDefensePanel()`, `renderInboxPanel()`, `pollInboxCount()`, `showAsyncComparison()`
- `blindspot-flow.js`: `startAsyncBattle(defenderId, isRevenge)` reuses matchmaking overlay, calls `ArenaAPI.startAsyncBattle()`

**Storage (Azure Blob):**
- `blindspot/defenseQueue.json` — global queue (max 500 entries, auto-prune 7 days)
- `blindspot/asyncResults/{userId}.json` — per-user inbox (max 50)
- `blindspot/profiles/{userId}.json` — `defenseCardId` field tracks which card is on defense
